content: 1. Jones M and Larson E conducted a study in 2003 that examined the duration of normal labor in women of Hispanic origin, published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health. 2. Schiff E, Cohen SB, Dulitzky M, Novikov I, Friedman SA, Mashiach S, and colleagues compared the progression of labor in twin versus singleton pregnancies in a 1998 study published in the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology. 3. Kilpatrick SJ and Laros RK Jr. described the characteristics of normal labor in a 1989 article in Obstetrics and Gynecology. 4. Lee SW, Yang JH, Cho HJ, Hong DS, Kim MY, Ryu HM, and colleagues investigated the effects of epidural analgesia on labor progression and perinatal outcomes in a 2007 study published in the Korean Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology. 5. Schorn MN, McAllister JL, and Blanco JD explored the impact of water immersion on labor in a 1993 study published in the Journal of Nurse Midwifery. 6. The WHO-CHOICE unit provided cost estimates for service delivery in a file accessed on March 29, 2017, detailing health service cost-effectiveness. 7. Lowe NK reviewed factors associated with dystocia and cesarean section in nulliparous women in a 2007 article in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health. 8. Nystedt A, Högberg U, and Lundman B conducted a case-referent study in 2005 on the negative birth experiences associated with prolonged labor, published in the Journal of Clinical Nursing. 9. Nystedt A, Högberg U, and Lundman B also explored Swedish women’s experiences of prolonged labor in a 2006 study published in Midwifery. 10. Bonet M, Oladapo OT, Souza JP, and Gülmezoglu AM conducted a systematic review in 2018 on the diagnostic accuracy of the partograph alert line, though the study remains unpublished. 11. Wei S, Wo BL, Qi H-P, Xu H, Luo Z-C, Roy C, and colleagues compared early amniotomy and oxytocin use for preventing or treating delays in the first stage of spontaneous labor with routine care in a 2013 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 12. Bedwell C, Levin K, Pett C, and Lavender DT conducted a realist review in 2017 on the effectiveness of the partograph for labor monitoring, published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 13. Ollerhead E and Osrin D reviewed barriers and incentives for partograph use in obstetric practice in lowand middle-income countries in a 2014 systematic review published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 14. Dujardin B, De Schampheleire I, Sene H, and Ndiaye F evaluated the value of alert and action lines on the partogram in a 1992 study published in The Lancet. 15. The World Health Organization (WHO) Maternal Health and Safe Motherhood Programme reported on the application of the WHO partograph in labor management in a multicenter study conducted between 1990 and 1991, accessed on January 17, 2018. 16. Van Bogaert L examined the outcomes of partogram use and neonatal outcomes in a 2006 study published in the Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology. 17. López CA conducted a comparative study in 2008 between the CLAP partogram and the WHO partogram in pregnant women at the Vicente Corral Moscoso Hospital in Cuenca, Ecuador, as part of a university thesis. 18. Orji E evaluated labor progress in nulliparous and multiparous women using the modified WHO partograph in a 2008 study published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics. 19. Rocha IM, de Oliveira SM, Schneck CA, Riesco ML, and da Costa AS analyzed the partogram as a tool for evaluating care during labor and delivery in a 2009 study published in Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da USP. 20. Diarra I, Camara S, and Maiga M assessed the use of the partogram in a district maternity hospital in Bamako, Mali, in a 2009 study published in Mali Médical. 21. Sanyal U, Goswami S, and Mukhopadhyay P examined the role of the partograph in spontaneous labor outcomes in a 2014 study published in the Nigerian Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology. 22. Bolbol-Haghighi N, Ebrahimi N, Delvarian Zade M, and Hasani MR evaluated the WHO partogram alert line for predicting Apgar scores at one minute after birth in a 2006 study published in the Journal of Shahrekord University of Medical Sciences. 23. Rani U and Laxmi B studied the impact of partographic monitoring on outcomes for women in spontaneous labor at term in a 2016 article published in the International Archives of Integrated Medicine. 24. Souza J, Oladapo OT, Fawole B, Mugerwa K, Reis R, Barbosa-Junior F, and colleagues found that cervical dilation over time is a poor predictor of severe adverse birth outcomes in a 2018 diagnostic accuracy study published in BJOG. 25. Fahy M, Doyle O, Denny K, McAuliffe FM, and Robson M analyzed the economics of childbirth in a 2013 study published in Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica. 26. Khan A and Zaman S compared the costs of vaginal delivery and cesarean section at a tertiary-level public hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan, in a 2010 study published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 27. Armstrong N and Kenyon S explored women’s experiences of delayed labor in a 2017 study published in Health (London). 28. Kobayashi S, Hanada N, Matsuzaki M, Takehara K, Ota E, Sasaki H, and colleagues assessed early labor support for improving birth outcomes in a 2017 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 29. McNiven PS, Williams JI, Hodnett E, Kaufman K, and Hannah ME conducted a randomized controlled trial in 1998 on an early labor assessment program, published in Birth. 30. Hofmeyr GJ, Mancotywa T, Silwana-Kwadjo N, Mgudlwa B, Lawrie TA, and Gülmezoglu AM audited a new model of birth care for low-risk pregnancies in South Africa in a study published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 31. Neal JL, Lamp JM, Buck JS, Lowe NK, Gillespie SL, and Ryan SL compared outcomes of nulliparous women admitted in preactive versus active labor in a 2014 study published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health. 32. Bailit JL, Dierker L, Blanchard MH, and Mercer BM compared outcomes of women presenting in active versus latent labor phases in a 2005 study published in Obstetrics and Gynecology. 33. Mikolajczyk RT, Zhang J, Grewal J, Chan LC, Petersen A, and Gross MM studied the effects of early versus late labor admission on labor progression and cesarean risk in nulliparous women in a 2016 article published in Frontiers in Medicine. 34. Chuma C, Kihunrwa A, Matovelo D, and Mahendeka M compared labor management and obstetric outcomes among women admitted in latent versus active labor phases at Bugando Medical Centre in Tanzania in a 2014 study published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 35. Holmes P, Oppenheimer LW, and Wen SW examined the relationship between cervical dilation at initial labor presentation and subsequent interventions in a 2001 study published in BJOG. 36. Tilden EL, Lee VR, Allen AJ, Griffin EE, and Caughey AB conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of latent versus active labor hospital admission for low-risk term women in a 2015 study published in Birth. 37. Mekonnen MG, Yalew KN, Umer JY, and Melese M identified determinants of delivery practices among Afar pastoralists in Ethiopia in a 2012 study published in the Pan African Medical Journal. 38. Dhakal S, van Teijlingen E, Raja EA, and Dhakal KB explored skilled care at birth among rural women in Nepal in a 2011 study published in the Journal of Health, Population, and Nutrition. 39. Kumbani L, Bjune G, Chirwa E, Malata A, and Odland JO investigated why some women fail to give birth at health facilities in rural southern Malawi in a 2013 study published in Reproductive Health. 40. Atuoye KN, Dixon J, Rishworth A, Galaa SZ, Boamah SA, and Luginaah I examined transportation barriers to accessing maternal and child healthcare services in rural Ghana in a 2015 study published in BMC Health Services Research. 41. Kowalewski M, Mujinja P, and Jahn A assessed the affordability of maternal healthcare costs in rural Tanzania in a 2002 study published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health. 42. Choulagai B, Onta S, Subedi N, Mehta S, Bhandari GP, Poudyal A, and colleagues identified barriers to using skilled birth attendants’ services in midand far-western Nepal in a 2013 study published in BMC International Health and Human Rights. 43. Chandhiok N, Shrotri A, Joglekar N, Chaudhury N, Chaudhury P, and Singh S explored the feasibility of partograph use by practitioners of Indian systems of medicine (AYUSH) in a 2015 study published in Midwifery. 44. Pattinson R, Cuthbert A, and Vanneval V reviewed pelvimetry for fetal cephalic presentations at term in a 2017 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 45. Rozenholc AT, Ako SN, Leke RJ, and Boulvain M studied the diagnostic accuracy of external pelvimetry and maternal height for predicting dystocia in nulliparous women in a 2007 study published in BJOG. 46. Liselele HB, Boulvain M, Tshibangu KC, and Meuris S evaluated maternal height and external pelvimetry for predicting cephalopelvic disproportion in nulliparous African women in a 2000 cohort study published in BJOG. 47. Devane D, Lalor JG, Daly S, McGuire W, Cuthbert A, and Smith V compared cardiotocography with intermittent auscultation of fetal heart rate for fetal well-being assessment during labor in a 2017 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 48. Lewis D, Downe S, and the FIGO Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring Expert Consensus Panel provided guidelines on intermittent auscultation in a 2015 article published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics. 49. WHO recommendations for preventing and treating maternal peripartum infections were accessed in a 2018 report. 50. Alfirevic Z, Devane D, Gyte GM, and Cuthbert A reviewed continuous cardiotocography as a form of electronic fetal monitoring during labor in a 2017 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 51. Herbst A and Ingemarsson I compared intermittent versus continuous electronic monitoring in labor in a 1994 randomized study published in BJOG. 52. Vijgen SM, Westerhuis ME, Opmeer C, Visser GH, Moons KG, Porath MM, and colleagues analyzed the cost-effectiveness of cardiotocography plus ST analysis of the fetal electrocardiogram compared with cardiotocography alone in a 2011 study published in Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica. 53. Chaturvedi S, De Costa A, and Raven J evaluated the Janani Suraksha Yojana cash transfer program for promoting facility births in India in a 2015 qualitative study published in Global Health Action. 54. Maimbolwa MC, Ransjo-Arvidson AB, Ng’andu N, Sikazwe N, and Diwan VK conducted a pilot study on routine care for normal deliveries in Zambian maternity wards in a 1997 study published in Midwifery. 55. Delvaux T, Ake-Tano O, Gohou-Kouassi V, Bosso P, Collin S, and Ronsmans C assessed the quality of normal delivery care in Côte d’Ivoire in a study published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health. 56. Walker DS, Shunkwiler S, Supanich J, Williamsen J, and Yensch A examined labor and delivery nurses’ attitudes toward intermittent fetal monitoring in a 2001 study published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health. 57. Martis R, Emilia O, Nurdiati DS, and Brown J reviewed intermittent auscultation of fetal heart rate during labor for fetal well-being in a 2017 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 58. Mugyenyi GR, Atukunda EC, Ngonzi J, Boatin A, Wylie BJ, and Haberer JE evaluated the functionality and acceptability of a wireless fetal heart rate monitoring device in rural Uganda in a 2017 study published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 59. Best practices in managing epidural analgesia in hospital settings were outlined in a report accessed in 2018. 60. Anim-Somuah M, Smyth RM, and Jones L compared epidural versus non-epidural or no analgesia in labor in a 2011 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 61. Thomson G, Feeley C, Hall Moran V, Downe S, and Oladapo OT reviewed women’s experiences with pharmacological and non-pharmacological pain relief methods for childbirth in a 2018 unpublished study. 62. Huang C and Macario A analyzed the economic considerations of providing adequate pain relief for women in labor, comparing epidural and intravenous analgesia in a 2002 study published in PharmacoEconomics. 63. Bernitz S, Aas E, and Øian P conducted an economic evaluation of birth care in low-risk women, comparing midwife-led and standard obstetric units in a 2012 randomized controlled trial published in Midwifery. 64. Tracy SK and Tracy MB estimated the cost of increased obstetric intervention in childbirth using population data in a 2003 study published in BJOG. 65. Bonouvrie K, van den Bosch A, Roumen FJ, van Kuijk SM, Nijhuis JG, Evers SM, and colleagues conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of routine versus on-request epidural analgesia during labor in a 2016 study published in the European Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology and Reproductive Biology. 66. Dillaway H and Brubaker SJ explored how women from different social locations discuss epidural use in a 2006 study published in Race, Gender & Class. 67. Sanders R examined functional discomfort and shifts in midwifery paradigms in a 2015 study published in Women and Birth. 68. Ullman R, Smith LA, Burns E, Mori R, and Dowswell T reviewed parenteral opioids for maternal pain management in labor in a 2010 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 69. Lamvu G, Feranec J, and Blanton E provided an update on perioperative pain management for obstetrician-gynecologists in a 2017 article published in the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology. 70. Dyer O reported on Ontario’s plans to stop funding high-dose opioids in a 2016 article published in BMJ. 71. Linge-Dahl L, Vranken M, Juenger S, North K, Scholten W, Payne S, and colleagues identified challenges to opioid availability and accessibility in Europe in a 2015 study published in the Journal of Palliative Medicine. 72. De Lima L, Pastrana T, Radbruch L, and Wenk R conducted a cross-sectional pilot study in 2014 to monitor the availability, prices, and affordability of opioids globally, published in the Journal of Pain and Symptom Management. 73. Lally JE, Murtagh MJ, Macphail S, and Thomson R reviewed women’s expectations and experiences of pain relief in labor in a 2008 systematic review published in BMC Medicine. 74. Gibson E explored women’s expectations and experiences with labor pain in medical and midwifery models of birth in the United States in a 2014 study published in Women and Birth. 75. Smith CA, Levett KM, Collins CT, and Crowther CA reviewed relaxation techniques for pain management in labor in a 2011 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 76. Smith CA, Levett KM, Collins CT, Dahlen HG, Ee CC, and Suganuma M reviewed massage, reflexology, and other manual methods for pain management in labor in a 2018 Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 77. Herman P, Poindexter B, Witt C, and Eisenberg D reviewed the cost-effectiveness of complementary therapies and integrative care in a 2012 systematic review published in BMJ Open. 78. Paterson CM, Saunders NS, and Wadsworth J described the characteristics of the second stage of labor in 25,069 singleton deliveries in the North West Thames Health Region in a 1992 study published in the British Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology. 79. Abdel Aleem H developed nomograms of cervical dilation and characteristics of normal labor in Upper Egypt.
